findings.title: Empty data passed to Prisma updateMany
findings.body: The new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`. Prisma requires at least one field in the data argument; an empty object is rejected by validation or performs no update. This runs at the end of `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` after availability has already been cached, so a validation error would fail the webhook cache refresh and cause retries/error handling, while a no-op would not actually refresh `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` or remove the call if the update is not needed.

findings.title: cacheUpdatedAt may be null/undefined when passed to Date constructor
findings.body: Although this JSX is inside the `hasCache` branch, TypeScript does not narrow the separate `cacheUpdatedAt` prop from the boolean local. The prop is `Date | null | undefined`, so `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` is a strict null check type error and will fail type-check/build. Verify the value directly, e.g. use `cacheUpdatedAt && ...`, or format in a helper that accepts `Date | null | undefined`.

findings.title: Delete cache mutation does not invalidate the connected calendars query
findings.body: After `deleteCacheMutation` succeeds, it shows a toast and calls `onSuccess`, but unlike `disconnectMutation` it never calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. The calendar list is rendered from a suspense query with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so after deleting cache the old `cacheUpdatedAt` can remain visible until a manual refresh. Add invalidation to the mutation's `onSuccess` or `onSettled` so the cache status is refetched.

findings.title: ENV_FILE path is relative to cwd and updates the wrong .env from repo root
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is interpreted relative to the caller's current working directory, not the script location. The likely invocation from the repository root, `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, resolves to the parent directory of the repository, so the tunnel URL is written to the wrong `.env` or a new file is created there. Compute `SCRIPT_DIR` from `BASH_SOURCE` and derive the path from that, or use a path relative to the repository root consistently.

findings.title: macOS-only sed -i syntax breaks on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux, including WSL and many CI runners, the empty argument is treated as a backup extension or an invalid option, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` line fails. Use a portable form such as `sed -i -E` under GNU sed, `perl -pi -e`, or detect the OS before choosing the syntax.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on npx fetching an undeclared tsx package
findings.body: The script was changed to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not declared in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` for this package. `npx` can fetch the latest `tsx` from the registry at runtime, which makes the dev script non-deterministic, may fail offline, and may not work correctly under Yarn PnP. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke the local binary, or use the already-declared runner.
